title: Recursive junta learner cost bounds
statement: Let $n,k\in\mathbb{N}$, let a relevant-coordinate finder for dimension $n$ and junta size $k$ provide a random-example learner with declared sample and work bounds, and let $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$ be a Boolean function. For a failure parameter $\delta\in(0,1/2]$, every outcome in the support of the recursive learner's run on $f$ uses at most $T_k B(\delta/T_k)$ random examples, makes no membership queries, and has charged work at most $T_k W(\delta/T_k)$, where $T_0=1$, $T_{r+1}=1+2T_r$, and $B,W$ are the finder's declared sample and work bounds.
hypotheses_covered: a relevant-coordinate finder for n and k
a Boolean target function on the n-dimensional sign cube
a learning parameter δ with 0 < δ ≤ 1/2
the outcome lies in the support of the recursive learner's run on the target
